text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on May 5. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- 16-year old singer Maarja-Liis Ilus won 82 points and eighth place for Estonia at the Eurovision song contest.
- The fight for power in Tallinn began again after mayor Robert Lepikson was appointed interior minister.

- An Estonian-Russian border agreement is nearly complete and may be signed in the near future, Russian border guard chief Alexander Nikolayev said at a meeting of Estonian, Russian and Finnish border guard leaders.
- Blind people in Tartu continue to protest against a decision of the Estonian Blind People Union to rent part of their house.
- Swiss investors are interested in starting a Eurolotto satellite TV in the Estonian town of Paldiski, formerly a Soviet military base.
- A sex shop in the south Estonian town of Viljandi moved into a back room of a handicraft shop after local authorities prohibited the display of pornographic material.
- Tartu Brewery will become the official importer of Pepsi drinks in Estonia; an agreement was signed in April.
